literal: Looking at her bracelet, looking also at her soft shoulders, looking at her feet, that was what she did there.
translation: She looked at her bracelets, she looked at her soft shoulders, and she looked down at her feet; that was all she did there.
modern: தன் வளையல்களைப் பார்த்து, தன் மென்மையான தோள்களையும் பார்த்து, தன் பாதங்களையும் பார்த்தாள்; அவள் அங்கு செய்தது அதுவே ஆகும்.
explanation: In this couplet, the hero interprets the silent, expressive gestures of his beloved. By looking at her bracelets ('toṭi'), she hints at her fear that they will grow loose and fall off due to the physical wasting caused by separation. Her gaze at her soft shoulders ('mentōḷ') expresses concern that they will lose their fullness, and looking down at her feet ('aṭi') signals her desire to accompany him. Through these three quiet glances, she communicates her deep anxiety about his impending departure without uttering a single word.
